stem:
Fig. 8.1 shows the lowest four energy levels of an electron in an isolated atom.

[[fig:f1]]

Fig. 8.2 shows the lines in the emission spectrum of the atom that correspond to the transitions of the electron from *n* = 3 to *n* = 1 and from *n* = 4 to *n* = 1.

[[fig:f2]]

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, with reference to photons, why there is a single frequency of electromagnetic radiation that corresponds to each of these transitions.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: On Fig. 8.2, draw a line that corresponds to the transition of the electron from *n* = 2 to *n* = 1. Label this line A.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: On Fig. 8.2, draw a line that corresponds to the transition of the electron from *n* = 3 to *n* = 2. Label this line B.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The frequency of radiation represented by line A is *f*ₐ.
The frequency of radiation represented by line B is *f*ᵦ.
The energy of the ground state (*n* = 1) is *E*₁.

Determine an expression, in terms of *f*ₐ, *f*ᵦ, *E*₁ and the Planck constant *h*, for the energy *E*₃ of the energy level *n* = 3.

figures.caption: Fig. 8.1
figures.alt: Four horizontal energy levels labelled *n* = 1 to *n* = 4 are shown beside an upward arrow labelled increasing energy.

figures.caption: Fig. 8.2
figures.alt: Two horizontal lines show emission-spectrum lines, with an increasing-frequency arrow pointing to the right.
